By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 06:28.

It has been revealed that in recent seasons, Manu Kone has often been linked with Paris Saint-Germain, but the capital club have never really tried to sign him. The reason behind that choice has been revealed.

It has been revealed that A talented French international from the Paris region, Manu Kone seemed to have the ideal profile to join PSG. The Roma midfielder has often been reported on the capital club's shortlist, but PSG have never really tried to recruit him.

The 25-year-old will return to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday at 8pm UK time, for matchday five of the Champions League with the Italian side.

He will have the chance to show the full extent of his talent to Parisian supporters, although it is unlikely that Kone will join the two-time European champions in the short term, according to L'Equipe.

The sports daily tried to explain the reasons for PSG's choice not to sign the French midfielder. This summer, Paris simply had no desire to recruit another midfielder and wanted to count on their current squad, with its established players such as Vitinha and Joao Neves, and its young gems such as Dro Fernandez and Senny Mayulu.

Sources indicate that paris had an opportunity in the summer of 2024. Before his move to Roma for £15.3m (€18m), the Frenchman was offered to Paris. Some people internally pushed for the capital club to sign this promising and affordable young box-to-box midfielder. Luis Campos has always liked the profile of the former Toulouse player.

However, PSG decided otherwise. 'I do not make all the decisions on my own' - the Paris sporting director remarked.

In a recent development, L'Equipe concludes that Luis Enrique did not approve the option. The Spanish boss preferred to rely on his Neves-Vitinha-Ruiz trio. Therefore, unless he changes his mind, the Kone option appears to be one to forget in Paris.

In a recent development, while PSG appear to have moved on, Kone has regularly been linked with clubs in England. Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United were all credited with interest in the Roma midfielder during the summer transfer window, including on deadline day, according to the Liverpool Echo.

In a recent development, chelsea were noted to still have an interest in late August, with Kone one of several midfielders on their list, according to CaughtOffside. At that stage, the website considered Manchester United effectively out of the race after the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, although that was its own assessment rather than a reported club position.

More recently, Gazzetta dello Sport reported in mid-November that Chelsea could make a move in January. Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini reportedly vetoed a sale in the final hours of the summer window, and the Italian club are noted to value Kone at £47m-£51m (€55m-€60m), compared with the £43m reported in August.

Opinion: Liverpool can solve two problems with incredible double transfer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool have many problems that they need to solve among their ranks.
  • Andoni Iraola's men are fourth in the Premier League table at the moment with seven points separating them and first-placed Arsenal.
  • Manchester City and Brighton are the two other teams ahead of them with one point between all three clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have many problems that they need to solve among their ranks.

Andoni Iraola's men are fourth in the Premier League table at the moment with seven points separating them and first-placed Arsenal.

Manchester City and Brighton are the two other teams ahead of them with one point between all three clubs.

Liverpool's rocky start to the season really didn't help matters much and is one of the main reasons why they are where they are right now.

However, with the January transfer window now just around the corner, Liverpool could take advantage of it and force their way back up the table.

Barcelona want to sell Gavi and Alejandro Balde in January.

Two of the main positions that the Reds need to upgrade this winter are their left-back and centre-midfield.

Both positions have players among them that haven't met expectations at all this term.

This has led to a lot of underperformance from Liverpool and has forced them to continually experiment with the players that they have at their disposal.

In some cases, players such as Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas have massively benefitted from this but, in others, questions remain.

Many different players are on the Reds' shortlist but now, an patch from journalist Juan Jesus may have just confirmed who the Reds' main targets could end up being.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other.".

Gavi and Alejandro Balde would be two perfect signings for Liverpool.

Most Liverpool fans will know that Balde has been linked with the Reds for a while now.

The Spaniard has been left out of Hansi Flick's intends this term with the La Liga giants making it clear since the summer window slammed shut that the 23-year-old had no future left at the Camp Nou.

His natural position is left-back but, he's also been used as a right-back in the past.

Gavi is a completely different kettle of fish altogether. The 22-year-old has played in 179 games throughout his career so far with his best position being a central midfielder.

During his time in Barcelona's first-team squad, he's helped Pedri boss many different midfields and has contributed to 28 goals across all competitions.

Right now, it's unclear how much either of them would cost but, since the Reds' relationship with Barcelona is strong, a deal could definitely be agreed.

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:10.

Real Madrid produced a sensational second-half comeback to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with England star Jude Bellingham proving instrumental after being introduced at half-time.

Recent findings suggest that jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

Bellingham's influence attracted widespread praise from the Spanish media, with several publications describing him as the decisive figure in Madrid's transformation.

His 45-minute contribution included a goal, an assist and a series of impressive individual statistics.

AS were particularly impressed, publishing the headline "Bellingham: lo cambio todo" - 'Bellingham changed everything'.

Manu de Juan highlighted how the England international reorganised Madrid's midfield, allowing Arda Guler to operate deeper and giving the hosts greater control and attacking momentum. AS also praised his spectacular volley for the 2-1 lead and his subsequent assist for Vinicius.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

David Alvarez argued that Madrid's first-half performance had been lifeless and directionless, with Bellingham's introduction restoring clarity, composure and quality. His spectacular volley was described as a beautiful and devastating goal, with the newspaper suggesting the Englishman's arrival completely transformed the contest.

Mundo Deportivo labelled Bellingham a "superestrella" - 'superstar' - and suggested that he is at the moment Madrid's best player, while highlighting how his introduction changed the game.

In a recent development, elDesmarque were equally enthusiastic, awarding the midfielder 9/10 and naming him their MVP. They highlighted his immediate influence, spectacular goal and assist for Vinicius, describing his 45 minutes as an outstanding exhibition.

It has been revealed that real Madrid-focused publications Defensa Central and madridistaReal went even further, awarding him 10/10 and 9.5/10 respectively. Both considered his introduction the turning point in Madrid's victory.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER also marvelled at his volley, with several commentators comparing the technical brilliance of the finish to something Zinedine Zidane might have produced - 'It's like Zizou,' one remarked.

Mourinho was equally impressed, describing the England international's performance as "absolutamente devastador" - 'absolutely devastating'.

In a recent development, the Portuguese coach explained that he had initially considered leaving Bellingham out to protect him from fatigue, believing Madrid could win without him. However, he admitted that having the midfielder available from the bench proved decisive.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

The statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played important roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

Sources indicate that receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. His goal may have been the highlight, but it was his all-round contribution that made this one of his most impressive performances of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alisson Becker, Liverpool's undisputed first-choice goalkeeper, is into the final year of his deal at Anfield.

The Brazilian has become an iconic figure in Merseyside, with many believing he is one of the best 'keepers the club has ever had, but his time in between the sticks in L4 is now coming to an end.

Negotiations are reportedly taking place that could see the shot-stopper stay put for at least another year, but Alisson's age and injury record indicate that the Reds will need a replacement within the few years anyway.

Several top candidates have been shortlisted, but the club have now been warned that they could miss out on one top target.

Liverpool told they will miss out on transferOne of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move as a potential successor to Alisson is Bart Verbruggen, who has been a standout at Brighton this season. The Dutch international has kept 12 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Seagulls already, and is rapidly becoming one of the most sought-after 'keepers in world football. One of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move as a potential successor to Alisson is Bart Verbruggen, who has been a standout at Brighton this season.

The Dutch international has kept 12 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Seagulls already, and is quickly becoming one of the most sought-after 'keepers in world football.

Verbruggen is on Liverpool's shortlist, but Real Madrid look set to beat the Reds to the24-year-old's signature.

That's according to a report from Football Insider, in which former Everton chief executive Kieth Wyness explained that he believes the Dutch 'keeper's preference is to move to Madrid.

"I've got a funny feeling that the auction for a keeper like [Verbruggen] may mean that Liverpool might not be the winners," Wyness remarked. "I think Verbruggen might be looking at a club in Spain; that's my feeling.".

The report names Real Madrid as the Spanish club that could land Verbruggen over Liverpool, but doesn't completely rule out the Dutchman making a move to Merseyside.

It is unclear how much Brighton will demand for their goalkeeper, but the battle for his signature is sure to heat up as the season comes to a close.

#118440. Industry News: Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1725 w)

Industry News: Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.
  • Sources indicate that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert big chances when the time comes.
  • Sources indicate that I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.

Sources indicate that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert big chances when the time comes. And the way the team is starting games after the break is worrying, with teams who are battered to within an inch of their lives early on suddenly able to compete.

Sources indicate that I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog. One where I’m miserable, of course: the players can’t shoot, they make all the wrong choices in the decisive moment, we can’t keep wasting chances and dropping off after the break, if Andrea Berta doesn’t deliver the true heirs to Thierry Henry and Robert Pires in January, then he should be stuffed into one of the cannons outside the Armoury and fired into the cold night air.

The other version is much more glass half full: Arteta is coaching masterclasses every week, this level of dominance in games is something I could only dream of a few years ago, that’s the most shots we’ve had in a game all season, we’re top of the league, we’re creating loads without any set-piece reliance and without Bukayo Saka – the goals will come.

Sources indicate that some people reading this would prefer (and relate better to) one version, and others the other version, I’m sure. Let’s see where we end up!

Sources indicate that there were, as there tends to be in these Champions League games, a fair few changes from the weekend. Kepa, Piero Hincapie, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis, and Viktor Gyokeres all came into the team.

In a recent development, despite featuring half a different side, there were plenty of parallels with the Newcastle match. Arsenal were dominant from the off, with Hincapie and White taking turns to play off of Gyokeres. Dortmund had no idea how to cover them and both fullbacks were the targets of early crosses into the box.

After a couple of long-range efforts, Arsenal got their goal they deserved, with Gyokeres launching a ferocious, dipping effort beyond Gregor Kobel. The Swede can put his foot through the ball, that’s for sure, and the Dortmund backline gave him the sort of time and space to set himself that he doesn’t often get.

The pressure continued after the opener for a while, with Tzolis forcing a good save and Madueke just unable to sort his feet to tap in the rebound.

It’s fair to say the game settled down after 15/20 minutes, with Dortmund growing into it a little, but it was still Arsenal who looked like scoring the next goal. Rice shot over from almost the same patch of grass Gyokeres had scored from, and the midfielder had another chance when a beautiful one-touch move ended with him bursting through, hurtling towards the Dortmund box. Maybe he could’ve picked out Madueke in support, but he went alone and Nico Schlotterbeck just got across to block the shot.

Another huge chance was denied by the offside flag as much as the finishing – Madueke won the ball high, Odegaard squared it to Gyokeres, and the Swede fired over from near the penalty spot. Odegaard was ruled offside but I’m not convinced: had the ball hit the net, I think we’d have seen a very tight VAR check.

In a recent development, there was one thought on everyone’s minds at half-time: don’t do the same thing again. After Slavia Prague and Newcastle, do not do the same thing again.

Arsenal did the same thing again.

Gyokeres was, by UEFA standards, lucky not to concede a penalty when a corner struck him on the arm. There was another early warning sign with Dortmund sliding the ball across the box and Maximilian Beier kicking the air. He didn’t make the same mistake with his next opportunity. Centre-back Joane Gadou (who was very impressive all evening) charged through the heart of the pitch before playing the ball to Beier, who jinked to unbalance Gabriel and slotted home.

Sometimes a goal is just a good goal, and I don’t think anyone was really at fault here. It’s a great run from Gadou, Beier tricks Gabriel to take the ball onto his weaker left side – it’s fair if Gabriel is expecting (and blocking the angle) on the attacker’s favoured foot, I know how that can happen. I think if we score that goal we’re talking about two brilliant individuals, rather than defensive errors.

My first thought? Not again. My second? OK, how do we respond? Because on Saturday, the response was poor.

This time it was a lot better. Jobe Bellingham had a rebound disallowed for offside, a moment that really brought the crowd back into the game, but in truth, that was Dortmund’s only real moment of threat. From the goal on 55 minutes to full-time, Arsenal had 15 shots to Dortmund’s two.

And that doesn’t include Serhou Guirassy playing one-twos with the post after a clever, low free-kick from Martin Odegaard late on.

Madueke had an effort blocked. Gyokeres flicked a header wide. Madueke shot wide beyond the far post after a good run. Gyokeres missed a massive chance with his head from six yards out. Rice hit the near post from a tight angle after a brilliant pass from Eberechi Eze.

A couple of late corners came to nothing, and that was it.

Mikel Arteta was clearly pleased with the performance on the whole:.

Recent findings suggest that well, I think I love the way the team played. There’s no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game … It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net. That’s my feeling.

to do what we’ve done out there is just something to be very, very pleased about, because there is very little more that we can demand from the team.

But we all know what that little more is:.

Industry observers note that obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn’t land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

According to recent reports, often when Arsenal don’t win games, it feels like it’s because the team haven’t created enough chances. We end up focusing on that one moment, where that one player didn’t execute the way you wanted. But last night wasn’t one of those: Arsenal didn’t struggle to turn dominance into good, slick football, and that football into a healthy number of decent opportunities.

In a recent development, that’s incredibly frustrating, but I do think you win a lot more often than not when you do that. Maybe that’s a hard sell for some this morning, but it’s how I feel about it when we play well, especially when we’ve been winning games anyway. That’s the first time this season we’ve gone two without a win across all competitions, and we’ve won 14 of 19 games so far. Sometimes things don’t fall for you, and this one felt a lot like ‘one of those’, certainly more than Newcastle did.

A word for a couple of promising performances too, with the boss asked about Gyokeres in his post-match press conference:.

What I love the most is how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threw it in behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the victory that we need.

Sources indicate that his finishing was off after the brilliant opener, but at least he was in the positions: too often this season and last, Gyokeres has gone through a game barely registering a shot. He had seven last night, and if he can do that more often he’ll score a lot more. His general play was improved too, both holding the ball up and competing in behind.

And I thought Martin Odegaard was excellent too. His eight chances created from open play was the most of any player in any Champions League match so far this season.

In a recent development, since we returned to the competition in 2023, we’ve had a player create more than five chances in a match just twice: Odegaard at Napoli in September (6) and Odegaard last night (9). He’s incredibly unlucky not to be leaving the game with a couple of assists.

Recent findings suggest that the draw leaves us in a decent position to finish in the all-important top eight in the league phase still, although you have to squint a bit to see us landing in the also-important top two. Real Madrid are up next and that’s a reminder of the sort of teams we’re up against: finishing in the top two is a tall order at the best of times.

Sources indicate that with each passing game, it is impossible not to wonder what could be done in January to add to the team. Unless there’s a sudden uptick out of nowhere, those thoughts aren’t disappearing. And even if there is a massive uptick, those thoughts will still be around. But 30 shots is the most we’ve had in a game all season, and the same group of players have scored more goals with fewer shots (/chances) plenty of times. Let’s hope we see some more clinical finishing on Sunday.

Guess I landed on the glass half full version.

Sources indicate that there should be an Arsecast once Blogs has caught up with the game, so stay tuned for that. Enjoy your Wednesdays!

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

If you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, it creates a short-term matter and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

Since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

Sources indicate that it’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

It has been revealed that it opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

Sources indicate that looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

According to recent reports, so far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

Now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

Sources indicate that no one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.
  • Recent findings suggest that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads.
  • According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a upcoming wave of signings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.

Recent findings suggest that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a upcoming wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

At present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

Should the fresh rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

According to recent reports, as well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

Sources indicate that it is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund declared a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

Because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

The Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

Self-serving Scottish clubs were always going to ensure Craig Mulholland's youth football revolution was doomed to failure

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Given how rapidly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.

Given how rapidly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

In a recent development, however, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a fresh head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those intends have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game.

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a upcoming watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those plans might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

But that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

In a recent development, it is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any latest proposals.

According to recent reports, the SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these plans through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

Industry observers note that but nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.

The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.

Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

However, subsequent scans proved positive, with the Spanish goalkeeper avoiding a serious injury and not requiring surgery.

There have been suggestions that Raya could only be sidelined for a matter of days and might therefore be in contention to face City, but Arteta was unwilling to offer any guarantees after the Dortmund draw.

"No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately," the Arsenal manager noted (via the Evening Standard). "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].".

Arsenal will therefore have to wait for further clarity on their first-choice goalkeeper, with Kepa potentially required to retain his place against Enzo Maresca's side, who also drew at home to Napoli this midweek.

Kepa produced a reasonably solid display in Germany, with Arteta describing his performance as "really good" and insisting that Arsenal fully trust their goalkeepers.

The Spaniard made three saves and received a 7.5 Sofascore rating, making him the Gunners' third-best performer on the night. His expected goals prevented figure of 0.38 also reflected a positive contribution.

Recent findings suggest that there were, however, a few moments that offered cause for concern. Kepa was wrong-footed for Dortmund's goal, while he parried a disallowed effort back into a dangerous area and did not look as assured as Raya when dealing with crosses.

Arteta is nevertheless confident in his deputy, saying: "We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.".

It is encouraging that Kepa has Arteta's backing, but there would understandably be some apprehension about him starting against a side of City's calibre. Raya's command of his penalty area and reliability have made him an crucial figure for Arsenal, and his absence would be a significant setback.

However, if the first-choice goalkeeper is not ready, Kepa will have to step up when called upon.

Julian Ward and Andoni Iraola have a lot of work to do on Liverpool's first-team squad this January.

Over £150 million was already spent on the club this summer but, since they're currently fourth in the table and find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal, they have a bit of ground to make up.

Obviously, all of their problems can't be rectified in the winter window but, if they can fix some of their main ones, that would be spectacular.

Not only would bringing in another player or two give the Reds a boost but, it would also help them get back on track and start to get back to their best.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target' rather than a short-term option.

Over the last few days, the transfer rumour mill has been going into overdrive.

Every single position among the Reds ranks is being scrutinised with fans seemingly rather happy with the recent performances of their club.

On Sunday, they managed to beat Manchester United 4-0 and, even though the Red Devils were down to 10 men for most of the day, Liverpool's performance was still impressive.

However, their problem areas were made clear once again with only two strikers available for Iraola to choose from.

And, of the two, one of them was Lewis Koumas who, even though he's good, he doesn't really jump out as a Premier League-winning attacker.

Because of this, rumours about the future of Liverpool's attack have emerged with Monza's Gustavo Varela now appearing on the Reds' shortlist.

However, a recent report from Football Insider has clarified just how serious Liverpool are about bringing the Portuguese striker in.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform.".

Gustavo Varela is an interesting transfer for Liverpool to explore.

Varela is almost certainly a player that barely anyone outside of Italy will have heard of.

The Portuguese striker is the Serie A's current top goal scorer despite his team being in a relegation battle.

The strangest thing is that, he only just joined the Italian outfit during the 2026-27 summer transfer window for €2.5 million.

Before this term, he'd had a couple of poor seasons but now, he really seems to have come into his own despite only being 21 years old.

His age coupled with his keen eye for goal are two major boxes that Liverpool like to tick when looking for attackers and, if the fee that Monza want is reasonable, there's no reason why a deal couldn't be explored.

Obviously, there's no point going for him in January as, the Reds need to see how good Hugo Ekitike is first but, as a potential option for the future, Varela looks like a fairly solid option.

Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

Recent findings suggest that reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

Barcelona’s admiration for Porro is a reminder of the defender’s standing in European football, but there is currently no confirmed bid or formal approach.

According to recent reports, tottenham will be keen to retain a player who remains an notable part of their prepares. His long-term contract also means the club are under no immediate pressure to negotiate a sale.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48.
  • Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.
  • The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48.

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.

Maresca also acknowledged that his side are still searching for the right balance between attacking and defending following his arrival as Pep Guardiola's successor.

Maresca left Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye on the bench for the opening hour, while Phil Foden was also rested, prompting questions about his selection.

The City boss explained that his decisions were based on how he expected Napoli to set up, with the visitors having recently used a 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 formation.

"We expected Napoli to play 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 as they did in recent matches, so that would basically leave eight players in the middle, and hope to create more spaces down the wings," Maresca told Sky Sport Italia.

He wanted Rayan Cherki to operate out wide and exploit those spaces, although City struggled to turn their possession into enough chances during the first half.

Maresca also defended his decision to use Ayyoub Bouaddi in a deeper midfield role alongside Elliott Anderson, explaining that he wanted to maintain balance while allowing six players to attack.

However, the manager admitted that City's defensive shortcomings remain a significant concern.

"The main problem is that we are conceding too many goals, and we need to do something about that," he added.

Maresca also acknowledged that finding the right approach would take time, comparing City's transition to the challenges Arsenal and Manchester United experienced following the departures of Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson.

It is not unusual for Maresca to rotate his City side during midweek fixtures, but leaving Doku, Ndiaye and Foden out of the starting lineup for a potentially important Champions League match was still a notable decision.

City ultimately rescued a point, but the draw could prove costly in their hopes of progressing in the competition, particularly given their recent struggles for consistency.

Perhaps Maresca also had this weekend's showdown with Premier League title rivals Arsenal in mind, with City travelling to the Emirates for Sunday's late kick-off.

That is not to suggest the manager deliberately sacrificed the Napoli fixture, but resting Foden and keeping two dangerous wide players in reserve could indicate that he was considering the demands of a huge domestic encounter.

City need to find greater defensive stability regardless of the opposition, as Maresca himself acknowledged, but Sunday's meeting with the Gunners may have been a factor in how he approached his midweek selection.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola noted. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

Industry observers note that with the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two significant chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an vital moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite swiftly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Recent findings suggest that everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

“The performance was really good,” stated Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix.

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu.

Industry observers note that still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

According to recent reports, ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very promptly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

Industry observers note that there will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully launches it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

Sources indicate that A spell of Brighton pressure ends as Rutter can’t quite find Kostoulas with a low cross. The young striker stays down and replays show that Jacquet stood on his foot as the defender attempted a clearance. However, it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR. There wasn’t much in the challenge at all.

Sources indicate that kerkez scampers into Brighton’s box, reaching the byline, but he can’t dig out a cross as the chance disappears. Brighton will need to throw everything forward soon.

Now, that double change from Liverpool is here. Barcola and Isak depart to large applause, with Ngumoha and Koumas cheered on as they run onto the pitch.

According to recent reports, as expected, Rutter is on. He replaces Ayari, who will think back to his missed chance and shot off the post in the first half.

Gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Industry observers note that brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

According to recent reports, once again, Liverpool break through Gakpo. This time, it comes from a Brighton corner, but Gakpo’s cross for Isak at the back post is read by Dunk.

In his first involvement since entering the action, Nyoni ends a slick Brighton move by taking the ball off De Cuyper’s toe in the penalty area with a much-needed clearance. He seems to be limping after he was caught by De Cuyper.

The Reds were torn apart by the Turkish Super Lig outfit with former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt leading his team to a historic win.

Indeed, they are one of the better teams in Turkey but, compared to how much talent the Reds have among their ranks, they shouldn't have even had a chance to beat them.

That's why Liverpool's defeat was so hard to take for fans.

However, as mentioned, since then, things have gone well for Liverpool with the club even beating arch-rivals Manchester United 4-0.

Even though transfers are expected to occur in the January transfer window, Andoni Iraola still has a few players among his ranks who fans haven't seen the best of yet.

That's why Wednesday's Champions League tie against Club Brugge could be incredibly crucial for one of them.

Victor Munoz has to start against Club Brugge.

Sunday's game was Liverpool's highlight of the season so far.

Their win against the Red Devils meant that they were thrusted back into fourth position and now find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

This is still a decent gap to cut down but, it's a lot less daunting than the nine points that separated them over the international break.

During Sunday's victory against Man United, Victor Munoz was left on the bench to start with.

And, even though Liverpool were winning their arch-rivals 3-0 when the last 20 minutes of the game came upon them, Iraola still chose to bring the Spaniard on.

Most people expected that transfer to have been done to give those who started a rest but, Munoz had other aims.

In the 18 minutes of football that he played, his lightning quick speed and his ability to turn nothing chances into goals paid off as the 23-year-old bagged the Reds' fourth and last goal of the game.

He also maintained a 92 per cent pass accuracy and he even made one key pass.

This performance alone proves why he should be starting against Club Brugge in Liverpool's next Champions League tie.

Victor Munoz could become a key player for Liverpool in the next couple of years.

Munoz was Liverpool's bargain signing of the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard was brought in by the Reds for a fee worth around £35 million.

At the time, Newcastle were also trying to sign him but, in the end, he chose Liverpool.

Most fans thought that he'd be more of a back-up than anything else but, in reality, he's become a key member of Iraola's first-team squad.

His performances have been second to none and, even though he's often been used in his less preferred position of right-wing, he's still contributed to four goals in the 13 games he's featured in.

Here's hoping that, if Iraola does start the "outstanding" attacker on Wednesday, that he can put on another stellar performance.

However, any potential departure will depend on Mauricio Pochettino's assessment of the 29-year-old over the coming weeks.

Mazraoui has experienced mixed fortunes since joining United from Bayern Munich, with injury problems restricting him to fewer than 1,000 Premier League minutes last season.

His fitness has improved this term, and he has featured six times in the league, partly because of injuries to United's other full-back options.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Milan have discussed Mazraoui's profile with their transfer team as they consider defensive reinforcements under Amorim.

The Portuguese coach has regularly used a back four this season and could view the United defender as an attractive option because of his ability to operate on either side.

There is reportedly a belief that Mazraoui could 'pack his bags in January', with the Serie A giants potentially open to pursuing a deal.

However, everything hinges on Pochettino's plans for the player. The Argentine is yet to make a final decision, with the next few weeks expected to help determine whether Mazraoui is allowed to leave.

United have several areas of the squad requiring attention, and selling Mazraoui could provide Pochettino with additional funds to work with in January.

The Argentine is believed to have a budget of just £50m, with the club expected to make only two additions unless significant circumstances change.

With central defence, left-back and striker all potential priorities, every extra contribution to the transfer kitty could prove valuable.

Mazraoui has not consistently established himself in one position at Old Trafford, and a departure could benefit all parties if Milan are prepared to offer a reasonable fee.

United should not allow sentiment to get in the way of a sensible decision. If Pochettino does not see Mazraoui as an important part of his aims, cashing in during January could help fund reinforcements elsewhere.

There is still a decision to be made, but with multiple positions needing attention, every little helps.

In a recent development, one of the most significant details surrounding his future is a reported release clause worth around £50million. The clause is understood to allow him to leave Galatasaray for a club in one of Europe’s top four leagues, potentially giving Liverpool a clear route to pursuing a deal.

However, Galatasaray are reportedly pleased with their summer signing and have little desire to sell him so soon after his arrival.

It has been revealed that TEAMtalk also reports that Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, while PSG continue to be viewed as a possible destination. Both clubs could offer strong competition if Liverpool decide to turn their scouting interest into a concrete move.

His creativity and goal threat could make him an interesting option as the club continues to assess its long-term attacking aims.

For now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lewis Koumas has been a bit of a revelation for Liverpool.

The Welshman has joined up with the Reds' first-team squad thanks to the appointment of Andoni Iraola and his trust in youngsters.

When it was first revealed that Koumas would be staying with the Reds, most people thought he'd be the last option on the Spaniard's list.

However, he's somehow managed to become what looks to be his fourth or fifth-choice attacker.

Granted, most of his playing time has come as a striker but, he can also be used on either wing if needed.

But, with Hugo Ekitike returning and many different attackers now being linked with Liverpool, questions are being asked about what the future has in store for the 21-year-old.

Liverpool have added Gustavo Varela to their shortlist as a long-term target.

As mentioned, Koumas has been Isak's back-up so far this season.

The attacker has also been used in other positions but, when Ekitike is back in action, it's hard to see where and how the youngster is going to get a regular role.

That is, unless Ekitike comes back as a fraction of his former self, of course.

Obviously, Liverpool won't want that as they spent around £70 million on the Frenchman last term and, before his injury, he was probably their best player.

So, for Koumas, this season could be his last as a regular first-team option.

That is, especially after the latest transfer upgrade from Football Insider on Liverpool's pursuit of Gustavo Varela.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform.".

If Liverpool sign Gustavo Varela, there is going to be no room for Lewis Koumas.

Obviously, keeping Koumas a part of Liverpool's prepares is a major thing for Iraola at the moment.

His endless running coupled with his keen eye for goal have made him an excellent option for Liverpool to have at their disposal.

However, with someone such as Varela, who is already the Serie A's top goal scorer at 21 years old, there's going to be a lot of competition ahead of him.

Indeed, his recent links with Liverpool are just rumours at the moment but, if he continues with this purple patch of form for the entire season, most clubs from across the world are going to be interested in acquiring his services.

Right now, it's unclear exactly what the Reds blueprint to do with their squad but, the fact that they're already trying to sort their shortlist out for the future means that they must have a pretty accurate idea about what they want to do.

Here's hoping that the Reds sign enough players to make a difference to their team and actually improve it.

According to recent reports, his strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Industry observers note that pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

It has been revealed that the hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Sources indicate that referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Recent findings suggest that juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

According to recent reports, at his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti noted he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything key. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have a lot of work to still do on their squad.

Andoni Iraola took charge of the club just after they delivered an extremely shoddy title defence.

They ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League which resulted in them spending another £150 million on new players.

And, while some of those transfers have worked out, it still feels like one or two, such as Bradley Barcola, still have a lot to live up to.

Obviously, as each season goes on, clubs try to add new players to their ranks and, since Liverpool's Premier League title rivals will be doing this, the Reds need to figure out ways to improve their ranks and get back to their best.

Unfortunately, for some of Liverpool's players, this means that their time at Anfield will need to be brought to an end.

Liverpool want to sign Abdellah Ouazane.

On Monday evening, Anfield Watch revealed that Liverpool are eyeing a move for Abdellah Ouazane.

The 17-year-old is currently plying his trade for Ajax in the Eredivisie and, despite being so young, he's already featured in 20 games for the Dutch outfit this term.

During those games, he's contributed to eight goals across all competitions and he has also been played in an array of positions.

The Moroccan was properly promoted to their first-team squad this term after Mika Godts accepted a move to PSG.

Indeed, Ouazane did feature for Ajax once in their domestic cup last season but, this term is the first where he's been a regular part of Miguel Ángel Sánchez Muñoz's team.

To make the deal even sweeter and even more likely, Ouazane is actually a Liverpool fan so, if the Reds went in for him, there's very little chance that he'd say no.

Abdellah Ouazane joining Liverpool would confirm Harvey Elliott's exit.

Right now, Liverpool don't really have a proper back-up for Florian Wirtz.

The young German has been the Reds' number 10 for most of the season with James McConnell taking over the role in some of Liverpool's cup games.

And, while McConnell has done a decent job, it's clear that the Reds need to start thinking about having a genuine back-up for Wirtz among their ranks.

Harvey Elliott was probably hoping that would be his role this term but, instead, he's been sent out on loan again.

His time with Valencia started off fairly poorly but, now, he's finally starting to find his feet with his main goal for the campaign likely to be get back on the good side of Iraola.

But, unfortunately for the Englishman, who was often one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet, these recent links with Ouazane more or less confirm that his future lies away from Anfield.

That is, unless he can become Valencia's best player and start contributing to goals again.

Industry observers note that arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Industry observers note that chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:.

'Real Madrid played an exceptional game. Playing like that, they are serious contenders for the Champions League. They are improving enormously from week to week. Something is going on at Real Madrid, watch out!'.

In a recent development, after a start to the season marked by some turbulence, Real Madrid appear to have found their cruising speed. The spectacular win over PSV Eindhoven (5-1) in the Champions League confirmed that impression. Mourinho's side have just strung together a tenth consecutive victory in all competitions and have a perfect record in the Champions League, with five wins from five games. Above all, Real Madrid seem to have taken a step forward in their ability to turn games around.

The script against the Dutch side was far from straightforward. Trailing at half-time after a particularly worrying first half, Real Madrid looked a completely different team after the break. It was a reaction that bore the signature of their manager, who made three changes at half-time.

It has been revealed that the other massive positive of the evening was Jude Bellingham. Left on the bench at kick-off, the Englishman made a sensational entrance at half-time, to the point of transforming his side. His work rate, ability to get forward and influence between the lines immediately gave Real Madrid more options. His superb goal, scored after a remarkable piece of skill, rewarded a top-class performance.

Thierry Henry, again, was full of admiration:.

Recent findings suggest that '(Jude) Bellingham is incredible, the way he plays. Wearing the number 5 at Real Madrid is not easy, but he does it with astonishing ease. His personality is extraordinary. I cannot believe that some people doubted him in his own country. But he has silenced the sceptics with his current performances and proved to them that they were wrong at the World Cup. He always delivers with his attitude and his play.'.

Recent findings suggest that beyond his statistics, with seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances, Bellingham brings an extra dimension to Real Madrid's midfield. Mourinho therefore has a player capable of turning a game, but also of giving a real identity to the side's attacking play.

The Englishman's performance should not, however, overshadow Mourinho's decisions. At half-time, the Portuguese made a bold call with three changes: Bellingham, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen replaced Aurelien Tchouameni, Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao. It was a spectacular reshuffle, particularly at centre-back, where the two starters were punished after a difficult first half.

But there was also a desire to rebalance the side behind this choice. By installing Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in midfield, Mourinho prioritised technical control and ball circulation. Real Madrid were able to push their block up, press higher and regain control of the game. The manager also explained that he used several video clips during the break to correct his players' defensive and attacking mistakes.

According to Jamie Carragher on CBS:.

'Mourinho is building a fantastic team. Week after week, we see them improving. They lost to Atletico Madrid and we thought the season was over, but they managed to pull themselves together by beating Barcelona' - Carragher said.

The former Liverpool player's comments reflect an enthusiasm that now goes beyond the result of a single match. With a manager capable of changing the course of a game, a rediscovered Bellingham and a side gaining in coherence, Real Madrid are starting to look like credible contenders for the European title. At the same time, Paris Saint-Germain have lost two attacking options in Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

It has been revealed that the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

In a recent development, only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More vital for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

According to recent reports, that leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

Industry observers note that it ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti noted afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.
