Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

Recent findings suggest that but the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a substantial amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he stated.

Sources indicate that ‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a strategy to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ claims Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

In a recent development, ‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that reveals in his play,' notes Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

Recent findings suggest that nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against Fresh Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

According to recent reports, wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that demonstrates in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

It has been revealed that ‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In a recent development, in any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

In a recent development, juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

It has been revealed that the new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

Recent findings suggest that the visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

Recent findings suggest that the offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment aims.

In a recent development, the spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering latest players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

Lincoln City have sacked co-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The pair were promoted from the club's backroom staff after head coach Michael Skubala made the decision to leave the League One champions for Bristol City in the summer.

With Lincoln sitting in 21st place in the Championship table and two points above the relegation zone, a positive spin can be put on the club's first campaign in the second tier of English football for more than 60 years.

However, Tuesday's 4-0 defeat at Charlton Athletic was Lincoln's fifth successive loss in the Championship.

As well as one win and eight defeats being posted across a 10-match period, the club's hierarchy have decided for a change in direction.

A statement read: "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division.”   "We know how much this football club means to our supporters and are humbled by the level of support we’ve had home and away so far this season.".

ℹ️ City can confirm Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties as head coaches with immediate effect. We thank them for their contributions to the club over the last several years and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/mwLolWdxhp.

Lincoln add that they will next provide an enhancement on their search for a successor to Cohen and Shaw on November 30.

Despite 15 points coming from 17 matches, Cohen and Shaw can have no complaints over Lincoln's decision.

With Preston North End and Burnley - in 22nd and 23rd position - closing the gap, Lincoln's owners are justified in the move that they have taken.

Furthermore, second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers are the next visitors to the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Likely viewing that game as a free-hit under first-team coach Stuart Pearson, Lincoln will look to have a permanent manager in place for the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 13:05, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 13:05.

Liverpool are reportedly keeping a close eye on Borussia Dortmund youngster Joane Gadou.

The 19-year-old joined the German club in the summer transfer window from Red Bull Salzburg and has already made a strong impression at his new side.

The youngster has made 10 Bundesliga appearances, starting nine of them, while also featuring five times in the Champions League.

According to CaughtOffside's The Daily Briefing, Liverpool are among the clubs showing keen interest in the young centre-back, who is also capable of operating at right-back.

The Reds could face competition from Manchester United and Arsenal for Gadou, while Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also monitoring his progress.

Gadou is particularly strong in the air and has already produced several eye-catching performances, with his display in the 1-1 draw against Arsenal attracting considerable attention.

The report claims that although several top clubs are keeping a close watch on his development, none are currently ready to make a move for him.

The Frenchman is under contract at Dortmund until 2031, and while a departure could become a possibility at some point in the future, a move is not expected in the immediate term.

Liverpool will probably need to sign a fresh centre-back next summer, with Joe Gomez potentially heading for the exit.

With Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni, the Reds already have two highly talented young centre-backs, and there would be little harm in further strengthening their pool of promising defensive prospects.

Virgil van Dijk has been outstanding once again this season and is showing few signs that age is beginning to catch up with him.

Liverpool should certainly continue monitoring Gadou's progress for the remainder of the campaign, and if an opportunity arises, taking a chance on him as a potential long-term replacement for Gomez could prove worthwhile.

#118351. Is trust in science falling, or does it just feel that way?

Is trust in science falling, or does it just feel that way?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article is the third in a series discussing the results of Nature’s 2026 science-job satisfaction survey.
  • According to recent reports, iris Borowy thinks that teaching her postgraduate students how to tell fact from fiction is central to her job.
  • Sources indicate that borowy is one of the researchers who told a Nature survey earlier this year that they felt public trust in science had declined over the previous five years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Illustration: Gheleyne Bastiaen.

This article is the third in a series discussing the results of Nature’s 2026 science-job satisfaction survey. It’s the latest edition of such surveys, which started in 2010; the last two took place in 2018 and 2021. The 2026 survey, created in partnership with Thinks Insight & Strategy, a research consultancy in London, introduced in May and was advertised on nature.com, in Springer Nature digital products and through e-mail campaigns. It had 3,882 self-selecting respondents across 133 countries with 31% describing themselves as female and 19% as belonging to a minority ethnic group in their country of work. The full survey data sets are available at go.nature.com/4b2drrc.

According to recent reports, iris Borowy thinks that teaching her postgraduate students how to tell fact from fiction is central to her job. Yet some days, that work seems futile. “I feel silly teaching groups of eight people while, out there in the influencer sphere, complete idiots talk to millions,” says Borowy, a global-development historian at Shanghai University in China. “Granted, there are a lot of serious people doing good work online, but working against the propaganda is getting harder.”.

Sources indicate that borowy is one of the researchers who told a Nature survey earlier this year that they felt public trust in science had declined over the previous five years. Of around 3,900 respondents, 50% shared this view, with 33% thinking that trust had increased and 13% saying that it had stayed the same (see ‘Perceptions versus reality of public trust in science’).

Recent findings suggest that even though trust in science remains high overall, data from other surveys support the idea that trust levels have fallen slightly, after rising at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. A global survey of more than 140,000 people in 140 nations, published in October by the London-based funding charity Wellcome, found that the proportion of the public who trust science “a lot” or “some” declined from 80% in 2020 to 72% in 2025. Trust levels dropped below pre-pandemic levels in 5 of 14 regions: Australia and Latest Zealand, sub-Saharan Africa and central, western and eastern Asia. It rose in just two areas — western and southern Europe. In seven regions, including North America and northern Europe, it remained close to the 2018 pre-pandemic levels, when 77% of overall respondents expressed trust in science.

Nature’s survey data — which measure scientists’ perceptions of changes in public trust levels, not trust levels themselves — only partly match the trends in the Wellcome survey. In our self-selecting survey, respondents in Africa and Asia were the least likely to say that trust in science had dropped (28% and 34%, respectively). By contrast, 78% of respondents in North America and 64% in Europe thought that public trust had declined. Nature’s survey also revealed that perceptions of falling public trust colour scientists’ job satisfaction and influence who they think is ultimately responsible for rebuilding trust.

How the pandemic changed trust in science — in four charts.

How the pandemic changed trust in science — in four charts.

The mismatch between actual trust levels in North America and Europe, which remain relatively high, and some scientists’ impression that they’re markedly declining could be explained by a few things, notes Niels Mede, a science-communication researcher at Wageningen University in the Netherlands. One is that people who don’t trust science have become louder and more visible, particularly online, and that their messaging is making scientists feel threatened. This has driven a narrative in science media and policy debates of a “crisis of trust”, he says, which has fuelled the perception that overall trust is going down. In addition, he says, many scientists hold a pessimistic view of the public — seeing lay audiences as uninterested in and apathetic to science.

It has been revealed that there is also strong evidence that, in countries where scientists told Nature they felt trust in science had dropped, opinions about science are becoming more polarized along political lines. This is especially visible in the United States, where trust among right-leaning Republicans dropped sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic, whereas trust among left-leaning Democrats remained high. In the Netherlands, trust in science remains high overall but the proportion expressing low trust grew from 9.5% in 2019 to 14.6% in 2025. A UK survey published in April found that the proportion who trusted science “a lot” had dropped from 63% in 2020 to just 34%.

Given the gap between perceptions and realities when it comes to public trust of science, Mede claims that it’s important to read the trends in Nature’s survey “as a measure of how scientists experience their relationship with the public, not as a measure of public trust per se”.

Digging down into the country-level data from the Nature survey, it is clear that there are massive geographical differences in scientists’ perceptions of public trust.

In the United States, 83% of respondents felt that trust in science had decreased in the past five years, compared with 79% in Germany and 78% in the United Kingdom. By contrast, just 23% of respondents in India reported feeling that public trust in science had decreased, with a considerable majority — 61% — saying that they felt it had increased. In Japan, 37% of respondents felt trust in science has decreased, whereas 38% said it has stayed the same.

What’s the secret sauce for happy scientists at work? These eight countries offer some clues.

What’s the secret sauce for happy scientists at work? These eight countries offer some clues.

Sources indicate that nature’s findings from respondents in India closely match national data on public trust in science. In a survey across 68 countries published last year, India was the country with the second-highest trust in scientists after Egypt. Mede, who was one of the study’s authors, thinks that strong pro-science rhetoric from the Indian government could play a part in the country’s high trust levels.

The Indian constitution even lists developing a “scientific temper” — meaning one that is led by logic and evidence instead of belief or superstition — among the duties of its citizens. Mede states that Indian scientists might view this pro-science political climate as a proxy for public trust.

Nature’s survey data for Japan suggests that scientists there feel that public trust is relatively stable, even if the actual level of trust might be modest, notes Sotaro Shibayama, an economist of science at the University of Tokyo. This makes sense to him, because he thinks that science is less politicized in his country than it is in nations where a higher proportion felt trust had dropped. Studies indicate that trust in science fluctuates in Japan as well, Shibayama says, “but these fluctuations may be smaller than in countries where science has become more closely entangled with political and ideological divisions”.

It has been revealed that when asked what is driving the falling levels of trust, the responses indicate that scientists view distrust more as a problem originating externally, rather than something caused from within. Some 69% noted that misinformation was the main cause, followed by political pressure or influence on science (62%) and a lack of public understanding of science (54%). Survey-takers could select more than one driver and this question was asked only of those who answered that trust had declined.

According to recent reports, only 24% thought that increased scrutiny and scepticism of experts was a main driver of falling trust and just 23% thought that scientists’ communication with the public was to blame. “We often do not have training in science communication, nor do we really need it,” wrote one early-career Earth and atmospheric scientist in Portugal. “We are paid, and should be paid, to do science.”.

Recent findings suggest that have people stopped trusting science? The data tell a surprising story.

Sources indicate that have people stopped trusting science? The data tell a surprising story.

According to recent reports, but Mede says that the evidence that misinformation and a lack of public understanding erode trust significantly is “much thinner and more mixed than one would expect”. Shared values and transparency might matter more. A UK study published in September found that trust was shaped less by whether the public viewed scientists as experts and more by whether scientists were ‘on their side’. Perceptions of openness and transparency also mattered for trust, the study found: 73% of those with high trust in scientists agreed that scientists were generally open and transparent, compared with just 10% of those with low trust.

Misconduct and scientific fraud were not included among the reasons Nature’s survey-takers could select as drivers of falling public trust — an omission of the survey design, in hindsight. But in free-text answers, some respondents said that they felt scientists were partly to blame for public opinion turning against them. One social scientist in the United States wrote that “rampant fraud” in research, such as fabricated data and scientists racing to publish as much as possible with scant thought to the value of their research, has rightly drained public trust. He indicates that he feels “furious” that academics have undermined their own credibility. “I literally am embarrassed to tell people in my community what I do for a living,” he writes.

Sources indicate that another US respondent, an engineering researcher who said he comes from a cattle ranching family in Texas, wrote that academia “has earned every bit of scepticism that it receives from the public”. Most scientists don’t understand working-class people, he wrote. “When we use the degrees we earned at protected bubbles on university campuses to say that ‘we know best, give us power’, we have to accept that we are nearly always wrong.”.

Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

In a recent development, with just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

In stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin.
  • Sources indicate that moise Kean has suffered a fresh tibia injury in training with Como.
  • Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Sources indicate that moise Kean has suffered a fresh tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The latest problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s enhancement described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

Industry observers note that that initiative has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

In a recent development, for Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

Como 1907 is pleased to announce the signing of Italian international forward Moise Kean from @acffiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent.

— Como1907 (@Como_1907) September 1, 2026.

Luciano Spalletti’s side need results. Juventus sit six points behind fourth place and have averaged just over 1.6 points per game, according to Corriere dello Sport. The paper sees the run of fixtures as decisive for the push for a Champions League place. It warns that dropping points against Venezia would force Juventus to win every remaining game of 2026 to stay in touch with the top four.

The schedule offers little respite after the trip to Como. Juventus host Udinese on 6 December and Monza on 14 December. They then travel to Roma on 19 December.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The demonstration ended in the 71st minute, when Randal Kolo Muani converted a penalty to score the fourth and final goal of the match.
  • Manu Tournoux is a passionate and knowledgeable football enthusiast with a special focus on French football.

Juventus made short work of Venice this Sunday, on the occasion of the 12th day of Serie A. In front of their audience, the Bianconeri largely won (4-0), at the end of a one-sided second period. After a goalless first half, Nick Woltemade broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, before Teun Koopmeiners doubled the lead six minutes later (59th), on an assist from the first scorer. The Turinese then continued their offensive festival thanks to Juan Cabal, served by Edon Zhegrova (65th).

The demonstration ended in the 71st minute, when Randal Kolo Muani converted a penalty to score the fourth and final goal of the match. Four goals scored in just 18 minutes which definitively stunned the Venetians, unable to contain Turin’s offensives after the break. A clear and flawless success for the Old Lady, who returns to competition after the international break with a convincing victory.

A year ago, Raul Gonzalez Blanco left the fold. Legend of Real Madrid with whom he won 3 Champions Leagues and 6 Spanish championships, the 49-year-old had started a coaching career. Having moved to the youth teams of Casa Blanca, he held this role for 6 years, notably winning a Youth League during the 2019/2020 season. After several years where he had results, he applied to replace Carlo Ancelotti in the summer of 2025: “I’m happy to be here. I am where I want to be. When the time comes to assess the situation and the club makes decisions, if it ever makes them, which I don’t know, we’ll see.».

In a recent development, but in the summer of 2025, he left the Merengue club following the appointment of Xabi Alonso. Considered too soft by the Madrid management, Raul then slammed the door while waiting to find a first real challenge as number one coach. It was ultimately the Real Oviedo club which took the gamble by signing him a contract until June 2028. Relegated from La Liga last season, Real Oviedo is in ninth place, one point behind the play-off places. From a sporting point of view, there is nothing insurmountable about getting back into the race for promotion to La Liga. The problem mainly comes from the internal situation within the Asturias club.

According to recent reports, arriving within a squad whose contours he was unable to construct, Raul will have to quickly convince since Mexican businessman Jesús Martínez Patiño is quickly expecting a marked style of play from the Spanish technician. This was one of the reasons that pushed the leader to part ways with Julián Calero. In 4 years, 6 coaches have succeeded one another with Álvaro Cervera, Luis Carrión, Javi Calleja, Veljko Paunovic, Guillermo Almada and Julián Calero. An instability which has widened a gap between leaders and supporters.

The departure of Veljko Paunovic to bring back Luis Carrión last season in full operation to maintain La Liga was a moment of rift between the fans and the management. Additionally, Real Oviedo fans are often fans of FC Barcelona and Real Madrid. Through his attachment to the Merengue club, Raul represents a point of disagreement in the stands and will have to convince with the results. He will have to revitalize an offensive sector in difficulty with only 19 goals scored in 13 matches and big absentees like Carlos Fernández and Chris Ramos. A context far from easy for Raul who does not arrive on conquered territory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars.

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham.

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’.

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’.

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

Sources indicate that england manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team.

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America.

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

Sources indicate that he later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’.

While the Blues captain is still playing for Madrid, Mulumbu believes that a departure for the Premier League could be the next step in his career. “ I really think that after Real Madrid, if he wants to leave this club, and it’s a significant “if” because he will stay there for a long time, he will go to Liverpool, for sure “, he mentioned. The former Parisian therefore does not believe in a return of Mbappé to PSG, in particular because of the circumstances of his departure in 2024. “ It’s ironic because the way he left PSG wasn’t the best “, he recalled. To justify his prediction, Mulumbu relies above all on the links already established between the French international and the Reds. “ He spoke with Jürgen Klopp at the time and he is a real Liverpool fan. It would be the best option for him and for the club “, he added. A hypothesis which, however, remains very distant, with no departure from Real Madrid currently being announced.

This possibility did not come completely out of nowhere, since Kylian Mbappé himself admitted to having been close to joining Liverpool when he was still playing at AS Monaco. In an interview given to The Athletic last September, the French striker recounted the discussions initiated with Jürgen Klopp and his mother’s particular interest in the English club. “ Yes, I was close to Liverpool. My mother was a massive admirer of Jürgen Klopp and Liverpool was her favorite destination “, he confided. Fayza Lamari even went to Anfield to discover the facilities and meet the managers, before falling under the spell of the club. Mbappé also revealed that he met Klopp during a particularly original exchange, on board a plane, during which the German coach presented his project to him. “ I told him: ‘You don’t need to convince me. You are Jürgen Klopp, this is Liverpool, a great club’ “, mentioned the Frenchman. Despite these discussions, he ultimately favored PSG in order to win in his hometown. Now based at Real Madrid, where he is pursuing his goal of winning the Champions League and the Ballon d’Or, Mbappé therefore maintains a special history with Liverpool, even if there is no evidence today to confirm that he will one day join the Reds.

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19.

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites.

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the Latest York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder problem, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Breaking: Ayanna Howard thinks ‘everyone has to be part of’ building ethical AI tools

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that robotics researcher Ayanna Howard sees artificial-intelligence tools as an equalizer.
  • Rebooting the Machines: A Latest Human Vision for Artificial Intelligence Ayanna Howard Broadleaf (2026).
  • As artificial-intelligence tools upend the graduate job market, it might seem that there’s little for educators to be optimistic about.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that robotics researcher Ayanna Howard sees artificial-intelligence tools as an equalizer. Credit: Emma Parker Photography.

Rebooting the Machines: A Latest Human Vision for Artificial Intelligence Ayanna Howard Broadleaf (2026).

As artificial-intelligence tools upend the graduate job market, it might seem that there’s little for educators to be optimistic about. But AI and robotics pioneer Ayanna Howard, who is the president of Spelman College, a historically Black women’s university in Atlanta, Georgia, sees promise ahead.

Howard’s career has ranged from developing autonomous robotic systems at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory to serving as dean of the college of engineering at Ohio State University. She is a co-founder of Zyrobotics, a company that creates educational technologies for children who need extra support, and academic co-lead of Black in Robotics, an organization dedicated to making the robotics field more inclusive.

According to recent reports, in her book Rebooting the machines, Howard explains that the dangers of AI are real. Yet AI tools can improve people’s quality of life and create job opportunities — if humanity implements guard rails. She spoke to Nature about why she tells her students to embrace the technology, albeit with healthy scepticism.

I consider myself a realistic optimist. I’m positive about the possibilities of AI tools, but I realize that not everyone thinks the same way as I do — including some AI developers and companies in this space. We still need to do something to turn that optimistic viewpoint into reality.

If all types of individuals — those from various socio-economic backgrounds, races, genders and nationalities, and those that have disabilities, for example — all become part of the AI ecosystem, tools can be personalized. For instance, in health care, I want AI tools that are trained on my body composition, taking into account my age and the fact that I’m female. I don’t want a general model that was trained on men.

Industry observers note that I think so, but we have to be realistic about the fact that we currently have no guard rails in place. Our data can be scraped, so we have to protect our own information as individuals. I am optimistic about the future of data privacy, because companies are starting to consider paying people for their data. We pay artists to see their art and listen to their music, why doesn’t that happen for personal data?

Honestly, I’m optimistic about jobs. AI tools make knowledge much more accessible. For smart individuals who have not been trained as, say, a computer scientist, AI is an equalizer.

My advice is to have a healthy scepticism towards AI, but also to work out how to use these tools in your discipline and for your passions. Jobs are changing. For students starting university this year, I guarantee that when they graduate, the jobs available to them will be different to those that exist now.

I think that there is some fear, frankly, because some recent graduates don’t have jobs thanks to AI models accelerating the eradication of early-career roles. But the graduates who do get hired are those who know how to work with the AI tools that companies are throwing at them.

The ones that some people call soft skills, although I call them hard skills because AI models can’t replicate them. One of them is human curiosity, which leads to creativity. Also, people are really good at learning things for the first time, whereas AI needs tonnes of data to work anything out. That means humans are really good at dealing with anomalies.

Robots can be useful educational tools for children who have extra support needs.Credit: BSIP/UIG/Getty.

The other element is that many jobs still rely on human connection. AI tools are pretty useful for diagnosis in health care. But we still want a human to interpret the AI output and interact with us. Those jobs are going to be difficult to replace.

Recent findings suggest that studies have shown that the current generation of young people report high levels of loneliness, and yet they’re also more connected than previous generations. I think that at some point they will say, ‘you know what? I don’t like being lonely. I need human connection’. But if people feel that AI is making them less lonely — although there is evidence that it isn’t — there is a risk that they will take a long time to come to that realization.

Industry observers note that the other risk is that people begin to trust AI tools too much. Because AI models are getting so good, there is a tendency not to question them. For example, if an AI tool used in health care tells people something incorrect and they don’t examine it, that could be disastrous.

Industry observers note that the cost of hardware has gone down, and the time needed for a robot to learn what we call the action space — I see something, I work out how to do something and then I am able to actually do it physically — has shortened. That’s what’s required to operate in the real world.

In a recent development, you can’t ‘control–alt–delete’ harm to a human. With a virtual AI tool, if it completes a task, it’s not doing anything physically. (Although, as AI agents become more sophisticated, there’s a question of how much longer that will be the case.) Right now, a human still has to say ‘yes’, or confirm or click something to initiate a behaviour. When an AI model controls a physical system, you don’t necessarily have that feedback loop. That is a very risky scenario.

One answer is to collect more data. There are communities that don’t give their data to organizations training AI models because they know that their information could be used against them. But for applications that involve high risk but high return, we have to have a conversation about it. When a company tests a drug, people are willing to volunteer to take it and provide their data, because the benefits outweigh the risks. Can we do the same thing for some AI applications?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Organization, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

In a recent development, in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

According to recent reports, stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that swiftly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

Sources indicate that as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange newly introduced worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!".

Industry observers note that stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

Industry observers note that his parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Manufacturer, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

Stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in New York.

According to recent reports, in the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a new edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation.".

Recent findings suggest that the successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a big deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway.".

But his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

Sources indicate that in 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to concerns such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

In a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the Fresh York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

This series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the newly introduced head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Industry observers note that olympiacos are at the moment second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

Recent findings suggest that in the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey is the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical challenges, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

#118332. The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1171 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • It has been revealed that the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

It has been revealed that the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

Industry observers note that the plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Industry observers note that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of key artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Recent findings suggest that bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

Industry observers note that however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

The dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked major and dangerous.".

It has been revealed that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian says. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

The designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

It has been revealed that still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

The feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

"It's really crazy," she states, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:36.

Real Salt Lake will try to extend their season into next week with a Friday win over the Vancouver Whitecaps at America First Field in game two of that best-of-three playoff series.

The reigning MLS Cup runners-up captured game one 2-0 last Sunday, putting them one win away from round two in the Western Conference playoffs.

After surviving a nervy shootout in the Wild Card Round, Salt Lake are now on the brink of elimination yet again after a subpar showing in game one against the Caps.

On Sunday, Pablo Mastroeni’s men suffered just their second defeat in their last eight MLS outings and were second-best for much of the game.

While they are on the verge of another early exit, they can draw optimism from being unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs at America First Field.

During the regular season, Salt Lake indicated strong attacking potency on home soil, netting three or more goals six times and scoring multiple times on 12 separate occasions.

They will try to end a five-match playoff losing run on Friday, scoring a goal or fewer in each of those instances.

Claret and Cobalt have not lost a playoff match at home in 90 minutes this decade, with their only such victory at America First Field occurring on penalties versus the Houston Dynamo in game two of that opening round series.

It is just one game, but Vancouver looked very much like title contenders as they began the 2026 MLS post-season in style.

Jesper Sorensen’s side carried the play throughout game one and will seek a fifth consecutive MLS triumph on Friday.

While this is the fourth straight year the Caps are in the post-season, they have won only once in that span in normal time away from home, beating San Diego 3-1 in the Western Conference Final last year.

Meanwhile, they failed to win three of their final four regular-season away fixtures this season against Western Conference opposition, with the highest-scoring team in the West failing to score on two of those occasions.

Vancouver have never lost a playoff encounter under Sorensen when netting first but have also never won a post-season outing in 90 minutes when conceding the opener under his leadership.

Sorensen, meanwhile, has won every match against RSL as the Caps boss, including their last two visits to America First Field, in which his team scored three goals both times.

Vancouver Whitecaps Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a hamstring strain, Ariath Piol may miss this match for RSL, while Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are questionable because of knee injuries and Zach Booth still has to clear concussion protocol.

Sergi Solans has scored three goals in his last two MLS home outings, including the opener in their 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy on Decision Day, while Rafael Cabral kept game one close, making six saves, many of them spectacular.

On the Vancouver side, an illness may keep Belal Halbouni out on Friday, and it is unlikely we will see Kenji Cabrera feature as he deals with a foot injury.

Edier Ocampo got the Caps on the board late in the opening half of game one, with Bruno Caicedo adding some insurance in the final 45 minutes.

Real Salt Lake possible starting lineup:.

Cabral; Yedlin, Glad, Quinton, Engel, Sanabria; Lobjanidze, Guske, Spierings, Guilavogui; Solans.

Vancouver Whitecaps possible starting lineup:.

Takaoka; Ocampo, Blackmon, Priso, Johnson; Larraz, Cubas; Sabbi, Muller, Caicedo; White.

The Serie A disciplinary judge suspended no players after matchday 12, so neither Juventus nor Como lose anyone for Sunday's game. Como were fined again for a slow restart, and Juventus head to Lake Como five points behind them.

It has been revealed that juventus travel to Como on Sunday with no suspension worries. Nor do their hosts. Serie A disciplinary judge Gerardo Mastrandrea banned nobody after matchday 12 in a ruling published in Milan on 24 November.

In a recent development, the decisions covered the games of 21, 22 and 23 November. Nobody was sent off across the round. No player one booking from a ban picked up a yellow card either.

Industry observers note that juventus had no cards from their own fixture. The club’s match sheet for the 4-0 win over Venezia at the Allianz Stadium lists no bookings, with Arena as referee.

All four goals came after the break. Woltemade (53′), Koopmeiners (59′) and Cabal (65′) scored before Kolo Muani converted a penalty (71′).

Two Lecce players, Danilo Veiga and Jamil Siebert, picked up their fourth booking of the season and are now one caution from a ban, Virgilio Sport reported. No Juventus or Como player reached that threshold this round.

Sources indicate that como did not escape the judge entirely. The €8,000 fine was imposed under strict liability for delaying the start of the second half by about four minutes without good reason. The judge treated it as a repeated repeat offence.

In a recent development, it was the largest of the round’s penalties for late restarts. Fiorentina and Milan were also fined as repeat offenders. Genoa received €3,000 for a two-minute delay to kick-off.

The problem is not new for Como. In the previous round, the communiqué of 10 November fined them €10,000, again as repeated repeat offenders. On that occasion the second half started about two minutes late.

It has been revealed that juventus were not blameless that week. The same 10 November ruling fined them €5,000 for holding up the start of the first half by the same margin as Como’s latest delay.

The match carries weight in the race for the top four. Como have 8 wins, 2 draws and 2 defeats from their 12 games. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

Juventus have 6 wins, 3 draws and 3 defeats. Their attack, with 19 goals, has almost kept pace with Como’s. The difference lies at the back, where Juventus have conceded 12.

Industry observers note that A win on Lake Como would narrow the gap to their hosts. Defeat would push Juventus further from the top four.

Como host Juventus at the Sinigaglia on 29 November.

Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. The feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.
